correctness.rationale: For each particle grade, the creator and annihilator norms give a scalar nonnegative path-matrix upper bound. The scalar matrix splits into even/odd input parities. On either input parity explicit unit alternating left-tensor words make both neighboring output summands collinear with nonnegative coefficients, attaining that parity-block norm. Thus both bounds meet for every Hilbert dimension and every u,v, including complex phases. The zero-vector cases and N=0 are checked separately. Direct matrix multiplication gives two Jacobi blocks; in the equal-norm case the symmetric path sine eigenbasis yields exactly 2s cos(pi/(N+2)) and its quadratic deficit. Executable finite tests support, but are not used to establish, infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Particle cutoffs are an explicit mechanism of the motivating Fock norm-bound literature. Their Hilbert spaces grow exponentially with cutoff when dim H>1, but the mixed nonselfadjoint sharp norm always reduces to two finite Jacobi blocks of total size N+1, independent of creator-annihilator angle. The proof supplies constructive norming vectors and, at balanced lengths, an optimal quadratic finite-cutoff error with exact constant. This is a natural quantitative invariant and structural reduction beyond a textbook one-variable path eigenvalue.
